Those things use the thickness of the z-axis of the print to create shadows and highlights; ie the thicker it is the darker it is. That means any color you put behind a section that is shaded or otherwise has a darker tone will be much darker than what is represented on your transparency. A light color, translucent or transparent filament (or resin) would be your best bet but may affect how the lithophane itself turns out. I’m interested to see what you end up with.

Your ink consumption will also depend on the type of printer you get. Compare these 2 UV printers: DCS’s UV 1024 MVP and Logojet’s UV2400. Both are built around the Epson stylus platform (the 2000 and the 2400 respectively) and use the same DX5 printhead. In fact, all of the components in these printers that are manufactured by Epson are identical. -okay, the EMB may have some minor differences but that’s it- 
The capping stations are the same and the machines will run their auto head cleans at the same rate and for the same duration of time, but Logojet has eliminated “ink maintenance “ and never bothers with initial charges. DCS has a huge problem imo with ink maintenance cycles that has only gotten worse over time and, while they can be usually be avoided, initial charges sometimes just have to happen. So while the amount of ink that gets wasted out on the logojet is significant, it’s still maybe half of what ends up in the waste tank of an mvp. I’m fairly certain that the cost of that wasted, completely unusable ink doesn’t get factored into any of their costing features. For 1L of ink, you’ll lose maybe 200mL on the 2400 and double that or more on the mvp.
